subject: Experiment Beauty
method: Provisional acquisition-routing inventory produced from verified reads of the Capture handoff's immutable packet set. The read covered 717 readable Reddit post/comment records and the seven Sephora onboarding corpora, with owned, YouTube, GoPicky, and access-limit observations retained from the handoff. Overlapping observations were grouped only to nominate the material-exhaustion work; no origin-independence, prevalence, decision maturity, or final semantic conclusion is awarded here.

axes.label: Hydration, barrier support, and visible results
axes.scope: Super Saturated, Molecular Mesh, Buffer Jelly, Continuum, and the brand-level hydration/barrier promise
axes.customer_tension: Captured customers describe strong hydration and barrier comfort, while others describe short-lived hydration, increased dryness, or too little visible difference to repurchase.
axes.segment_or_condition: Dry or dehydrated skin, damaged barriers, cold climates, tretinoin routines, and combination skin.
axes.strongest_counterevidence: Multiple captured Reddit accounts describe Super Saturated or an Experiment multi-product routine as unusually effective for dehydration and overnight barrier comfort.
axes.known_gap: Separate product, skin-state, season, and routine effects; test independent support beyond the current retailer and known-source Reddit batch.

axes.label: Irritation, breakout, and active-condition fit
axes.scope: Reaction and tolerance reports across high-glycerin, moisturizer, cleanser, and occlusive products
axes.customer_tension: Some captured customers report burning, itching, whiteheads, eczema discomfort, or breakouts, while others describe soothing use on irritated or tretinoin-affected skin.
axes.segment_or_condition: Sensitive, acne-prone, eczema-prone, rosacea-prone, and retinoid-using customers.
axes.strongest_counterevidence: Captured community accounts describe Super Saturated and Buffer Jelly as soothing or useful in irritated and tretinoin routines.
axes.known_gap: Test product- and condition-specific segmentation without treating anecdotes as medical-safety or causal evidence.

axes.label: Texture, finish, layering, and routine fit
axes.scope: Stickiness, slime/stringing, absorption, pilling, shine, makeup use, and day/night fit
axes.customer_tension: The textures can make hydration feel distinctive and effective, but tack, slime, pilling, shine, or poor absorption can make the same products unacceptable in another routine.
axes.segment_or_condition: Makeup wearers, oily or combination skin, dry skin, layered routines, and people using products at different times of day.
axes.strongest_counterevidence: Captured comparisons praise Molecular Mesh's bouncy texture and describe tack as useful under makeup or manageable through layering changes.
axes.known_gap: Determine which texture consequences change purchase or routine behavior and which are merely preference language.

axes.label: Packaging, dispensing, and physical durability
axes.scope: Tubes, pumps/nozzles, reusable-mask durability, refill utility, and usable product loss
axes.customer_tension: Customers can like the formula or packaging concept while reporting failing nozzles, hard-to-use containers, small fill, or a reusable mask tearing after very little use.
axes.segment_or_condition: Repeat users, travelers, customers judging usable quantity, and reusable-product buyers.
axes.strongest_counterevidence: Other captured users praise the packaging or refill option, and some continue using products despite dispensing complaints.
axes.known_gap: Test recurrence by product and packaging version, and distinguish aesthetic praise from reliable dispensing and durability.

axes.label: Price, value, quantity, and access
axes.scope: Price-to-result, usable quantity, refill economics, prestige alternatives, and US/Canada purchasing routes
axes.customer_tension: Some customers accept the price for unusual hydration or formula feel, while others see a familiar substitute, too little product, or too little difference to justify repeat purchase.
axes.segment_or_condition: Budget-sensitive repeat buyers, cross-border shoppers, prestige switchers, and customers comparing functional substitutes.
axes.strongest_counterevidence: Captured repeat-purchase accounts describe certain Experiment products as unusually effective or economical in use because a small amount is sufficient.
axes.known_gap: Separate generic price objection from observed switching, refill value, and access-driven purchase friction.

axes.label: Formula consistency, quality, service, and brand trust
axes.scope: Ingredient-list conflict, batch/scent observations, contamination allegations, response handling, and confidence in brand standards
axes.customer_tension: Captured sources include strong formula praise alongside differing official ingredient lists, batch/scent concerns, and a customer account linking a foreign-material allegation with an unresolved support interaction.
axes.segment_or_condition: Ingredient-sensitive buyers, repeat users noticing batch differences, and customers needing remediation after a quality concern.
axes.strongest_counterevidence: Captured community accounts also praise the formulations and report good use without adverse reaction; the official ingredient mismatch is unresolved source content, not proof of a formula change.
axes.known_gap: Resolve current formula/version identity and seek independent recurrence or successful remediation without promoting a single allegation into prevalence or causation.

axes.label: Repeat purchase, rejection, and switching destinations
axes.scope: Executed retention, return, replacement, and named competitor or substitute destinations
axes.customer_tension: The captured corpus contains enthusiastic retention and routine reliance, but also returns and named moves driven by texture, reaction, value, or product-performance fit.
axes.segment_or_condition: Customers with direct comparative use and an expressed purchase or routine consequence.
axes.strongest_counterevidence: Several captured users call Super Saturated indispensable or describe the Experiment routine as their best overnight routine.
axes.known_gap: Distinguish executed destinations from comparison mentions, resolve the triggering tension, and test whether behavior repeats across independent origins.

axes.label: Portfolio, product selection, and routine fit
axes.scope: Choosing and combining Experiment products by skin state, desired intensity, routine slot, and product category
axes.customer_tension: Captured users describe coherent multi-product routines and strong hero products, while product boundaries and category expansion can also produce mismatch or uneven confidence across the portfolio.
axes.segment_or_condition: New-to-brand buyers, multi-product users, sensitive or dry skin, makeup routines, and lip/body-category shoppers.
axes.strongest_counterevidence: Captured users explain purposeful stacking of Super Saturated, Molecular Mesh, and Buffer Jelly and describe differentiated uses across routine slots.
axes.known_gap: Test whether the portfolio ladder is legible and whether weaker categories dilute or materially change trust in the hero-product proposition.

excluded_or_merged_provisional_axes.reason: Strongest delight is a required counterweight within every material axis, not a separate customer tension.
The current access evidence is routing context and has not yet shown a distinct customer-behavior axis.
The present service signal is tied to one quality allegation; separate service recurrence has not yet been established.

claim_ceiling: This inventory routes acquisition. It is not prevalence, causation, medical-safety, market-consensus, final semantic adjudication, decision maturity, or axis-closure authority.
